layout_dets.text: INTRODUCTION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Nitrogen added to austenitic stainless steels improves their pitting and crevice corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance.1-6 Several mechanisms for the role of nitrogen in stainless steels have been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: suggested. Janik-Czachor et

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed that N forms carbonitrides of the type

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and as a consequence the number of high chromium containing carbide particles becomes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lower and thereby the sensitivity to pitting corrosion is reduced since pitting is often initiated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at the boundaries of carbide inclusions. Osozawa and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: found that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ions appear

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the aqueous solution after pitting tests of N-containing stainless steels. Jargelius and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Wallin6 have shown that the amount of NH‡ ions in the electrolyte corresponds to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: amount of N in the dissolved volume of the metal. Thus,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ions are formed by reaction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between N and protons when the passive film is locally broken and the metal is dissolved.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The reaction prevents lowering of the pH in the pits and may thereby enhance repassivation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It has also been proposed that a beneficial effect of N is obtained by a synergistic effect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The aim of this paper is to study the influence of N on initiation of pitting and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: repassivation of austenitic stainless steels polarized in hydrochloric acid. Two alloys with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the same composition, except for their nitrogen content, are analysed. The composition of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the reaction products is analysed by means of ESCA. A model for the synergistic effect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between Mo and N is suggested.

layout_dets.text: CONCLUSIONS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: High alloyed stainless steels, 20Cr-20Ni–6Mo, containing 0.011 wt% N and 0.19 wt%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: N have been exposed to 0.1 M HCl + 0.4M NaCl for 10 min and 2 h at potentials in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: range — 75–800 mV (SCE). It is concluded that:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Nitrogen influences markedly the pitting corrosion properties of the steels. At

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the low N-containing steel is severely pitted while the high N-containing steel is passivated.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. The shapes of the dynamic polarization diagrams of the steels recorded after

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: activation are the same and independent of the N content of the steel.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. The composition and the thickness of the passive films formed on the steels at room

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temperature are independent of the N content of the steel.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4. Nitrogen segregates anodically to the metal-oxide interface during passivation. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enrichment of N increases with the potential. The amounts correspond to 12% and 27% of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an atomic laver at — 75 and 800 mV (SCE), respectively. It is concluded that Cr nitride is not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formed.
